def Target : Prop :=
  d15.D10 ∧ ¬ ∃ N : S1 Bool Bool, N.D9 ∧ S1.D6 N d15

{"translation": "Target defines (without asserting or proving) a proposition consisting of a conjunction of two statements about finite-node Boolean-input, Boolean-output systems of type S1 Bool Bool and a particular system d15.

Here a system N : S1 Bool Bool consists of: a finite type of nodes N.A1; for each node n : N.A1, an arbitrary (not necessarily finite) state type N.A3 n; an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to every node n; a synchronous update function N.a5 taking a node n, a global state (an assignment of a state in N.A3 m to every node m), and an input x : Bool, and returning a new state in N.A3 n; and an output function N.a6 mapping a global state to Bool. On any finite list of inputs xs : List Bool, the system's output N.d4 xs is obtained by starting from N.a4, repeatedly updating all nodes simultaneously from left to right for each input in xs, and then applying N.a6 to the final global state. For nodes m, n : N.A1, there is a one-step dependency edge N.D8 m n if and only if there exist two arbitrary global states σ, σ' (not restricted to reachable states) and an input x : Bool such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x.

The specific system d15 : S1 Bool Bool has a single node (Unit) with state type Bool, initial state false, update rule mapping the current state σ () and input x to σ () || x (Boolean OR), and output function returning σ () (so on any finite list of Booleans, d15 outputs true if and only if the list contains at least one true, and false otherwise, including on the empty list).

Target is the proposition that both of the following hold:
1. (d15.D10) There exists a node n in d15.A1 (the unique element of Unit) that has a directed cycle of length at least 1 in the dependency relation d15.D8—that is, a chain of one or more d15.D8 steps from n back to n (a single self-dependency step counts; zero steps do not).
2. (¬ ∃ N : S1 Bool Bool, N.D9 ∧ S1.D6 N d15) There does not exist any system N : S1 Bool Bool (with any finite set of nodes and arbitrary, possibly infinite, per-node state types) that simultaneously satisfies:
   (a) Acyclicity (N.D9): for every node n : N.A1, there is no chain of one or more N.D8 dependency steps from n back to n (forbidding both self-dependencies and longer directed cycles); and
   (b) Full input-output equivalence with d15 (S1.D6 N d15): for every finite list xs : List Bool (of any length, including the empty list), N.d4 xs = d15.d4 xs."}
translation:
Target defines (without asserting or proving) a proposition consisting of a conjunction of two statements about finite-node Boolean-input, Boolean-output systems of type S1 Bool Bool and a particular system d15.

Here a system N : S1 Bool Bool consists of: a finite type of nodes N.A1; for each node n : N.A1, an arbitrary (not necessarily finite) state type N.A3 n; an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to every node n; a synchronous update function N.a5 taking a node n, a global state (an assignment of a state in N.A3 m to every node m), and an input x : Bool, and returning a new state in N.A3 n; and an output function N.a6 mapping a global state to Bool. On any finite list of inputs xs : List Bool, the system's output N.d4 xs is obtained by starting from N.a4, repeatedly updating all nodes simultaneously from left to right for each input in xs, and then applying N.a6 to the final global state. For nodes m, n : N.A1, there is a one-step dependency edge N.D8 m n if and only if there exist two arbitrary global states σ, σ' (not restricted to reachable states) and an input x : Bool such that σ k = σ' k for all k ≠ m, while N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x.

The specific system d15 : S1 Bool Bool has a single node (Unit) with state type Bool, initial state false, update rule mapping the current state σ () and input x to σ () || x (Boolean OR), and output function returning σ () (so on any finite list of Booleans, d15 outputs true if and only if the list contains at least one true, and false otherwise, including on the empty list).

Target is the proposition that both of the following hold:
1. (d15.D10) There exists a node n in d15.A1 (the unique element of Unit) that has a directed cycle of length at least 1 in the dependency relation d15.D8—that is, a chain of one or more d15.D8 steps from n back to n (a single self-dependency step counts; zero steps do not).
2. (¬ ∃ N : S1 Bool Bool, N.D9 ∧ S1.D6 N d15) There does not exist any system N : S1 Bool Bool (with any finite set of nodes and arbitrary, possibly infinite, per-node state types) that simultaneously satisfies:
   (a) Acyclicity (N.D9): for every node n : N.A1, there is no chain of one or more N.D8 dependency steps from n back to n (forbidding both self-dependencies and longer directed cycles); and
   (b) Full input-output equivalence with d15 (S1.D6 N d15): for every finite list xs : List Bool (of any length, including the empty list), N.d4 xs = d15.d4 xs.

divergences.description: Relative to P2's informal mention of "recurrent" and "feedforward systems", `S1 Bool Bool` idealizes systems as deterministic, discrete-time, synchronous, time-invariant (non-plastic) systems with finitely many units (`Fintype A1`) and Boolean inputs/outputs. P2 does not explicitly require finiteness of units or time-invariance, although finiteness of units is necessary for the counterexample and matches "static FNNs regardless of their size" in [P-O2].

Feedforwardness (`N.D9`) is defined via acyclicity of the one-step functional dependency graph (`N.D8`) quantified over all global states (including unreachable ones), while `N : S1 Bool Bool` allows arbitrary (possibly infinite) per-node state types and arbitrary update and readout functions. Evaluating dependency over unreachable states slightly restricts what counts as feedforward compared to a reachable-state notion (though it is broader than fixed structural wiring), whereas allowing arbitrary state types and functions strengthens the non-existence claim relative to standard weighted FNNs.

Relative to [P-O2], `Target` does not formalize general RNNs, weighted neural architectures, or persistent perturbations in hidden states, nor does it address approximate replication; instead, it instantiates the temporal-persistence impossibility via a single concrete one-unit Boolean latch (`d15`) and exact input-output equivalence over all finite Boolean sequences (`S1.D6`).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the claimed unbounded-horizon counterexample to P2—a single static, recurrent one-unit Boolean system whose input-output map over all finite sequences cannot be matched by any finite-unit acyclic synchronous system—and bears appropriately on [P-O2]'s claim about static FNNs. The only divergences are minor modeling idealizations (deterministic, discrete-time, finite-unit, all-states functional acyclicity) and the restriction to exact input-output non-replicability of a single Boolean latch rather than general weighted RNNs.
